subtopicTitle: Mechanization equations — integrating IMU to get position, velocity, attitude

cards.front: What two quantities does a strapdown IMU directly measure?
cards.back: Specific force vector $f^b$ (from accelerometers) and angular rate vector $\omega^b_{ib}$ (from gyroscopes), both expressed in the body frame.

cards.front: State the purpose of the mechanization equations in inertial navigation.
cards.back: They are the differential equations that integrate raw IMU measurements to propagate the navigation states: attitude $C^n_b$ (or quaternion), velocity $v^n$, and position $r^n$ (or latitude/longitude/altitude).

cards.front: Write the quaternion kinematic equation for attitude propagation from gyro measurements.
cards.back: $$\dot{q}^n_b = \frac12 q^n_b \otimes [0,\ \omega^b_{ib}]^T - \frac12 [0,\ \omega^n_{in}]^T \otimes q^n_b$$ where $\omega^n_{in}=\omega^n_{ie}+\omega^n_{en}$ is the transport rate.

cards.front: Give the velocity mechanization equation in the navigation frame (NED).
cards.back: $$\dot{v}^n = C^n_b f^b - (2\omega^n_{ie}+\omega^n_{en})\times v^n + g^n$$ (Coriolis, transport-rate, and gravity terms).

cards.front: How is position updated once velocity is known in the navigation frame?
cards.back: Latitude, longitude and height are obtained by integrating the velocity components after dividing by the local meridian and transverse radii of curvature: $\dot L=v_N/(R_M+h)$, $\dot\lambda=v_E/[(R_T+h)\cos L]$, $\dot h=-v_D$.

cards.front: Why must the measured specific force be rotated into the navigation frame before integration?
cards.back: Accelerometers sense force in the body frame; the navigation equations require the force resolved in the local-level frame so that gravity, Coriolis and transport-rate terms can be correctly subtracted.

cards.front: Derive the first-order attitude update for a small rotation vector $\Delta\theta$ over one IMU interval.
What additional term appears in the ECEF-frame velocity equation compared with the inertial-frame equation?
cards.back: The centrifugal acceleration term $-\omega^e_{ie}\times(\omega^e_{ie}\times r^e)$ must be included when integrating in the rotating ECEF frame.
